question_text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. When two dosage forms have equal tmax
B. AUC values of the two analogs can be compared to measure relative bioavailability.
C. Urinary data is valid to measure bioavailability.
D. Cmax is proportional to the rate of absorption.
List II:
I. When their total body clearance is constant.
II. Absorption rate constants are equal
III. When fraction absorbed and elimination rate is constant.
IV. Excretion of drug and/or metabolite is related to the bioavailable dose.

options.A: A - II, B -I , C -IV , D - III

explanation: Matching pharmacokinetic parameter relationships correctly links tmax to absorption rate constants, AUC to clearance comparability, urinary data to excreted bioavailable dose, and Cmax to absorption rate.

question_text: In pharmacokinetic models, the term "compartment" means
explanation: A compartment in pharmacokinetics does not represent a specific anatomical region or organ, but rather a hypothetical pool of tissue or fluid kinetically similar to one another.

question_text: The biological half- life of drug

options.A: It is a constant physical property of the drug
options.B: It is a constant chemical property of the drug
options.C: It may be increased in patients with impaired renal failure
options.D: It may be decreased in patients by giving the rapid IV injection

explanation: Renal impairment reduces the clearance of renally eliminated drugs, thereby increasing their half-life.

question_text: The area under the serum concentration time curve of the drug represents:

options.A: The biological half life of the drug
options.B: The amount of drug in the original dosage from
options.D: The amount of drug excreted in the urine

explanation: AUC is proportional to the total amount of unchanged drug that reaches the systemic circulation (bioavailability/absorption).

question_text: The area under the serum concentration time-curve represents the

options.A: Biologic half life of the drug
options.B: Amount of drug is cleared by the kidneys
options.D: Amount of drug excreted in the urine

explanation: AUC represents the total systemic exposure and extent of absorption of a drug.

question_text: When Ke is constant and Ka is larger:-

options.A: Cmax is more and tmax is longer
options.B: Cmax is lesser and tmax is longer
options.C: Cmax is lesser and tmax is short
options.D: Cmax more and tmax is short

explanation: A larger absorption rate constant (Ka) means faster absorption, resulting in a higher peak concentration (Cmax) achieved sooner (shorter tmax).
